weakest_line: And if you're here to stand for God's word, welcome to the Valiant.
one_fix: Open on the concrete puzzle (Israel saw the sea split and heard God at Sinai, and weeks later danced around a golden calf) instead of the abstract question, and drop the Schellenberg name-drop.

weakest_line: It's one of the most asked questions about the Bible and most Christians can't answer it.
one_fix: Replace the closing line 'you'll know what to say' with a real question that invites a response, such as whether 'every person you've ever met is family' changes how they see strangers.

weakest_line: Because it was the only thing standing between a family and death.
one_fix: Cut the Egypt backstory and actually answer the why from the text: Exodus 12:13 'when I see the blood, I will pass over you' (a substitute lamb dying in the firstborn's place), and Paul's 'Christ our passover is sacrificed for us'.

weakest_line: Some Christians also wonder about this question sometimes.
one_fix: Take on the hard half of the hook, 'forever', with specific textual evidence, rather than stringing together familiar verses about knocking and invitation.
Cut the colleague and job analogy and spend that time on the Peter and Judas contrast from the text, which is the strongest material.

weakest_line: People ask this in our comments all the time.
one_fix: Cut it to Cornelius plus one other answer. Three numbered answers, the Sodom digression and a survey of views are too much for a Reel and blur the payoff.

weakest_line: The change at home would be even more striking.
one_fix: Anchor the speculation in more text (for example the tree of life in Genesis 3:22 and its return in Revelation 22) so the picture of an unfallen world is shown from Scripture rather than imagined.

weakest_line: Let's look at Samson, known as the strongest man in the Bible.
one_fix: Cut the 'Let's look at Samson' line and open on the Gaza night itself (he slept with a prostitute, then that same night carried off the city gate), so the puzzle lands in the first seconds.
Open on the specific puzzle, 'God knew exactly where Adam was, so why did He ask Where art thou?', instead of a devotional question aimed at the viewer.

weakest_line: He knew Adam and Eve would disobey.
one_fix: Ground the answer in Genesis instead of hypotheticals about stealing and coveting, for example 'of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat' and the tree of life standing beside the forbidden one.
